# Aeoba

> Aeoba is a B2B Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), and Technical SEO agency based in Milan, Italy and Sliema, Malta. Website: https://aeoba.com. Contact: info@aeoba.com.

Aeoba is the agency entity and publisher. Our work connects buyer-intent questions, technical access, schema and entity engineering, evidence-led content, relevant external references, and dated citation measurement.

Implementation studies are illustrative workflows, not achieved client performance claims. Tool outputs are user-supplied scenarios or actual public-HTML checks, not independent verification of AI recommendations. Mentions, citations, referral visits, and qualified pipeline are distinct observations.

## Service plans and deliverables

- **Growth: $1,597/mo**. A managed program for one site and a focused set of commercial priorities. Technical and entity baseline for one website; 8 high-intent answer-engine pages per month with supporting media; 3–5 targeted brand mentions per month across Reddit, Quora, and industry best-of listicles, subject to editorial and community approval; Buyer-intent prompt mapping and weekly citation reporting.
- **Scale: $2,997/mo**. A broader managed program for a larger answer library and a wider set of buyer questions. Full-site technical and entity optimization; 15 high-intent answer-engine pages per month with supporting media; 5–8 relevant brand mentions per month, subject to editorial and community approval; Expanded buyer-intent prompt coverage and weekly citation reporting.
- **Enterprise: Custom**. An agency-led program scoped around your category, systems, and competitive requirements. Direct strategy and architecture with Aeoba; A custom prompt, entity, and measurement program; Content, technical, and authority work agreed at kickoff; Monthly strategy reviews and an inspectable delivery record.

Growth and Scale deliver 8–15 high-intent answer-engine pages/month and 3–8 targeted brand mentions/month across Reddit, Quora, and industry "Best Of" listicles, subject to fit, disclosure, and editorial/community approval. Programs include schema and entity engineering. Enterprise scope is agreed individually.

## 90-day citation guarantee

Ranked and cited in ChatGPT & Perplexity for at least 10 buyer-intent prompts in 90 days—or we keep working free until you are.

We agree on at least 10 relevant buyer-intent prompts at kickoff and record a dated baseline. A qualifying result is a named brand recommendation with a verifiable citation in both ChatGPT and Perplexity for each agreed prompt. The initial term is 90 days. You provide agreed access and approvals; if the agreed citation target is not met, our management work continues free until it is. You keep every page, schema update, and asset we ship.

When technical fixes, content, and authority work run independently, the most important buyer questions fall between teams. Aeoba connects the work to one agreed prompt set and a weekly execution rhythm.

- A 90-day roadmap tied to buyer intent
- Technical, schema, and content execution with your approval

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/services/technical-aeo

Aeoba reconciles visible business facts before adding markup, then validates the deployed implementation against the content a visitor can actually inspect.

Structured data cannot compensate for contradictory information. We reconcile visible facts, canonical URLs, named entities, and machine-readable markup before recommending additional schema.

- Crawlability and indexability baseline
- Organization, service, and page entity mapping

- A deployment and validation record

AI search analytics measures a defined panel of buyer questions through dated answer observations, named brand mentions, and inspectable citations. Aeoba records the engine, prompt, context, answer, and sources, then evaluates referral and commercial evidence separately so a citation is never presented as a visit or qualified opportunity.

AI answers vary by engine, date, context, and prompt wording. A useful baseline records those conditions and keeps the supporting answer and source, rather than presenting a single rank as permanent.

### AI Visibility Recovery

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/services/ai-visibility-recovery

AI visibility recovery starts by reconstructing when recommendations or citations changed and which pages, sources, or technical conditions changed with them. Aeoba checks access, entity consistency, content, and answer variability, prioritizes supported repairs, and repeats the original prompt panel before treating a suspected cause as an established explanation.

A change in visibility may come from an engine update, a site release, an altered source, or normal answer variability. We reconstruct the timeline before treating a correlation as a cause.

- A dated change and symptom timeline
- Indexability, entity, and content diagnosis
- Prioritized repairs with approval checkpoints
- Repeat observations against the original prompt set

## Complete AEO field guide

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/free-aeo-guide

Author: Aeoba

### 1. Define the buyer and the decision

Choose one offer, one audience, and a specific buying decision. Write down the facts a buyer needs to compare options. Separate product fit, implementation, pricing, and local availability so each question has a clear purpose.

Action: Write your primary offer and three buying questions.

### 2. Record an honest baseline

Run a stable prompt set in the engines you care about. Save the date, exact wording, context, answer excerpt, and sources. Record mentions and citations separately. An unchecked prompt is an unknown, not a failure.

Action: Save your first dated observation in the Answer Index.

### 3. Fix the technical foundations

Check titles, headings, canonicals, indexability, useful internal links, and mobile access. Make the business name, locations, contact details, and service facts consistent. Prioritize commercial pages before expanding the article library.

Action: Run the homepage readiness checker and list the first three repairs.

### 4. Publish useful, evidence-led answers

Answer the buyer's question directly, then support the answer with specific detail and firsthand evidence. Attribute substantive claims, explain limitations, and give the reader a next step matched to their intent. A comparison should help a buyer understand tradeoffs.

Action: Create an answer-page brief with the content workbench.

### 5. Describe the facts consistently

Add structured data that matches the visible page. Connect related entities with stable identifiers and canonical URLs. Only describe real locations, people, services, and claims. Keep FAQ markup synchronized with the questions a visitor can read.

Action: Generate and review an Organization or FAQ schema draft.

### 6. Earn relevant references

Contribute useful expertise where your buyers already look for evidence. Research editorial and community fit, disclose relationships, and keep a source log. Do not substitute distribution volume or manufactured endorsements for genuine relevance.

Action: Identify three relevant publications or communities and an original contribution.

### 7. Review evidence and decide what ships next

Repeat the agreed prompts and compare the results with the baseline. Add the work that shipped, the sources that changed, and the uncertainty that remains. Choose a small number of actions for the next week instead of chasing every fluctuation.

Action: Set a weekly review date and a priority for the next execution cycle.

## Complete research articles

### Build a buyer-intent prompt map before publishing another page

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/build-a-buyer-intent-prompt-map

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-22
Updated: 2026-11-23

Your next article may answer a question no qualified buyer is asking. A prompt map exposes that mismatch before you spend another week writing.

#### How do you build a buyer-intent prompt map?

Build a buyer-intent prompt map by collecting real customer decisions, grouping them by audience and buying stage, and assigning a primary page and evidence requirement to each question. Prioritize commercially useful gaps, record a dated answer baseline, and keep the original wording stable enough to compare later observations.

### Start with a decision, not a keyword list

Write down the decisions a qualified buyer makes before contacting you. Someone choosing a supplier may ask about capability, integration effort, price, alternatives, or location. Those questions have different evidence requirements. Grouping them into one broad topic produces vague content and an equally vague measurement plan.

Use sales conversations, support questions, and your own subject-matter expertise to draft the first list. Preserve the wording your customers use. Add the audience, decision stage, and relevant product or service beside each question.


### Choose prompts you can actually answer

A useful prompt has a clear connection to your offer and enough specificity to distinguish a useful answer from a generic recommendation. Include comparison, suitability, implementation, and commercial questions. Avoid padding the set with variations that ask for the same answer.

For each prompt, identify the page that should resolve the question. If no suitable page exists, record an evidence gap before commissioning a draft.

- Who is the buyer and what decision are they making?
- Which visible facts support your answer?
- Which page should own the topic?
- What useful next step should the reader take?


### Capture a repeatable baseline

Run the agreed prompts under documented conditions and keep the date, engine, answer excerpt, and sources together. Record a mention separately from a citation. An answer that names your business without linking to a useful source represents a different observation from a supported recommendation.

Answers can vary. A single favorable result is not a durable ranking. Repeating a stable set makes the evidence more useful without pretending that an answer engine behaves like a fixed search results page.


### Turn the map into an execution queue

Prioritize the prompts closest to a real buying decision, then assess the work needed to support them. The next action might be a technical correction, a clearer comparison page, a missing product fact, or an independent editorial reference. Publishing an article is only one possible response.

Review the map weekly. Keep the question set stable enough to compare observations, and record any deliberate changes so the next report explains what moved and why.


### Put the framework to work

Use Aeoba's [Managed AEO + SEO](https://aeoba.com/services/managed-aeo) to connect this framework to a scoped execution program. Start with the [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report) to identify the buyer questions and evidence gaps that deserve attention first.

#### Your first action

Choose one commercial question, assign its primary page, and record the evidence you have today. Agree on the next improvement and a date to review what changed.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### How many buyer prompts should we start with?

Choose a manageable panel covering distinct, valuable decisions. Start small enough to repeat checks and keep the evidence, then expand deliberately when a new question has a clear purpose.

##### Should every prompt have its own page?

No. Related questions may belong on one useful page. Assign a primary URL to each decision and create a new page only when it resolves a distinct information need.

##### How often should we update the map?

Review priorities weekly while keeping the baseline wording stable. Record changes to prompts and cohorts so later reports remain comparable.

### Useful schema starts with consistent facts

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/schema-without-contradictions

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-22
Updated: 2026-11-23

Perfectly valid JSON-LD can still describe the wrong business. One copied company name or outdated contact field can undermine the consistency your schema was meant to create.

#### What makes schema markup useful for AEO?

Useful AEO schema describes the same business facts a visitor can verify on the page. Reconcile names, canonical URLs, contact details, services, and locations first. Connect related entities through stable identifiers, validate syntax and vocabulary, and review the rendered implementation whenever the underlying content or business information changes.

### Reconcile the visible business first

Structured data describes a page; it should not introduce a different business. Check the name, canonical domain, contact details, locations, and service descriptions that a visitor sees. Reconcile inconsistent facts before adding more markup.

Choose a stable organization identifier and reuse it when describing the business on related pages. Distinguish the organization from individual people, products, services, and locations. Those entities are related, but they are not interchangeable.


### Use the simplest accurate representation

Start with the entities and properties you can support with visible, current information. An Organization record can describe the brand and connect its locations. A page-specific record should describe what the page actually contains.

Do not add ratings, certifications, offices, or awards simply because a schema generator offers a field for them. A technically valid claim can still be inaccurate.

- Use canonical URLs for identifiers and page references.
- Represent each location with its actual locality and country.
- Keep FAQ markup synchronized with questions visible on the page.
- Review changes when the underlying business information changes.


### Validate structure and meaning separately

Parsing JSON verifies syntax. A structured data validator can identify vocabulary and property problems. Neither step proves that the facts match the page or that an engine will display a rich result.

Review the rendered HTML and compare the markup with the visible content. Check duplicate organization records, conflicting canonical URLs, and accidental markup copied from a template. Preserve a small validation record with each release.


### Connect schema to a useful page

The strongest implementation is still attached to an answer a person can use. Clear headings, specific evidence, accessible content, and sensible internal links remain part of the work. Treat structured data as one consistent representation of that work rather than a substitute for it.


### Put the framework to work

Use Aeoba's [Technical AEO](https://aeoba.com/services/technical-aeo) to connect this framework to a scoped execution program. Start with the [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report) to identify the buyer questions and evidence gaps that deserve attention first.

#### Your first action

Choose one commercial question, assign its primary page, and record the evidence you have today. Agree on the next improvement and a date to review what changed.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### Does valid schema guarantee a citation?

No. Syntax and vocabulary checks establish implementation quality. The page still needs useful, accurate evidence, and engine citations require separate observation.

##### Which facts should we reconcile first?

Start with the brand name, canonical domain, public email, locations, and service scope. Compare the shared configuration, rendered pages, and JSON-LD.

##### When should structured data be reviewed?

Review it when business facts, templates, services, or content dates change. Include representative public URLs in release checks.

### A citation report should let you inspect the evidence

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/measure-citations-with-evidence

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-22
Updated: 2026-11-23

A dashboard says your AI visibility rose, but nobody can open the answer or its cited source. Without those records, the team cannot tell a real change from a reporting artifact.

#### How should a business measure AI citations?

Measure AI citations with a stable buyer-prompt panel and a dated record of each answer and source URL. Separate brand mentions, linked citations, referral visits, and qualified opportunities. Retain engine and conversation context, mark failed checks as missing, and connect the report to shipped changes and the next execution decision.

### Name the observation precisely

A brand mention, a linked citation, a referral visit, and a qualified enquiry are different events. A report becomes confusing when it presents them as one visibility score. Define each observation before selecting a dashboard.

Keep the engine, prompt, date, answer excerpt, and cited source together. Where a result depends on location, account state, or a particular conversation, record that context too.


### Keep a stable comparison set

Choose a manageable set of questions connected to real buying decisions. Repeat those questions on a documented cadence. Add new questions deliberately and distinguish them from the original baseline so the report remains comparable.

Do not convert unobserved answers into wins or losses. Missing evidence should remain missing evidence until the check is performed.

- Observed mention: the answer explicitly names the brand.
- Observed citation: the answer provides an inspectable source reference.
- Referral: analytics records a visit with available attribution.
- Qualified enquiry: the business applies its own agreed qualification criteria.


### Connect the report to shipped work

A useful weekly report includes the pages, schema changes, technical repairs, and editorial work that actually shipped. Link those changes to the prompts they were intended to support. Explain uncertainty rather than assigning every movement to the latest change.

A source may change, an engine may update, or an answer may vary. A dated record helps distinguish an execution problem from a measurement problem, even when it cannot establish a single cause.


### End with the next decision

Choose a small number of actions based on the evidence. You might improve an answer page, resolve an entity inconsistency, investigate a lost citation, or revisit a prompt that has little commercial relevance. The purpose of measurement is to improve the next allocation of effort.


### Put the framework to work

Use Aeoba's [AI Search Analytics](https://aeoba.com/services/ai-search-analytics) to connect this framework to a scoped execution program. Start with the [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report) to identify the buyer questions and evidence gaps that deserve attention first.

#### Your first action

Choose one commercial question, assign its primary page, and record the evidence you have today. Agree on the next improvement and a date to review what changed.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### Is a mention the same as a citation?

No. A mention names the brand; a citation provides an inspectable source reference. Record each separately, alongside whether the answer makes a relevant recommendation.

##### What should an observation contain?

Save the exact prompt, engine or product, date, available context, answer excerpt, source URLs, and result status. Keep technical failures separate from completed checks.

##### Can citations be counted as pipeline?

No. A citation is an observed answer event. Qualified opportunities need your commercial criteria and their own records, with attribution evidence preserved where available.

### Build authority without manufacturing endorsements

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/authority-without-manufactured-endorsements

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-22
Updated: 2026-11-23

A hundred mentions can add less buying evidence than one detailed, independent comparison. The difference is whether the reference helps a real prospect evaluate your offer.

#### How do you build credible off-site authority?

Build credible off-site authority by contributing original evidence or expertise where relevant buyers already look for information. Research editorial and community fit, disclose commercial relationships, and record the publication, context, and source URL. Treat published references and later observed AI citations as separate outcomes rather than manufacturing endorsements or inflating mention counts.

### Start with a contribution worth making

A relevant reference usually begins with something useful: firsthand data, a clear explanation, a working resource, or expertise that resolves a difficult question. Identify that contribution before building an outreach list.

Match the contribution to the audience. A specialist publication, a category comparison, and a community thread serve different purposes. A placement that looks impressive in a spreadsheet may be irrelevant to the people you want to reach.


### Make relationships clear

Disclose material relationships and respect a publication or community's rules. Do not present a paid placement as an independent recommendation, create fictional reviews, or impersonate a satisfied customer.

Community participation works best when the answer stands on its own. A link should add context or evidence rather than replace the contribution.

- Research audience and editorial fit.
- Check contribution and disclosure requirements.
- Provide original, reviewable material.
- Record the resulting source and its context.


### Measure relevance before volume

Track what the reference helps a buyer understand. Record the publication, audience, subject, relationship, and source URL. Keep earned editorial coverage separate from owned profiles and paid distribution.

An AI model may or may not cite a particular source. The useful claim is that the reference exists and contributes relevant evidence; an observed citation requires a separate engine check.


### Feed the learning back into your site

Questions and objections from an editorial conversation can reveal missing explanations on your own pages. Use those observations to improve your answer library, comparisons, and documentation. Authority work and content work should reinforce the same clear account of your expertise.


### Put the framework to work

Use Aeoba's [authority and community services](https://aeoba.com/services/authority-community-mentions) to connect this framework to a scoped execution program. Start with the [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report) to identify the buyer questions and evidence gaps that deserve attention first.

#### Your first action

Choose one commercial question, assign its primary page, and record the evidence you have today. Agree on the next improvement and a date to review what changed.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### What makes an external reference useful?

It should reach a relevant audience and provide specific, accurate evidence about a buying decision. Record its source, context, and relationship to the brand.

##### Can paid coverage be an independent endorsement?

A commercial placement should be disclosed and recorded as paid distribution. Keep it distinct from independent editorial recommendations.

##### How do we know a reference supports AI visibility?

First verify that the reference exists and is relevant. Count an AI citation only when a documented engine check actually returns that source.

### 60% of Searches End Without a Click—How B2B Brands Win the Citation Anyway

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/zero-click-search-b2b-aeo-citations

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-23
Updated: 2026-11-23

Your best prospect can learn your category, compare suppliers, and build a shortlist before your analytics records a single visit. If your only success metric is the click, the first half of that buying journey is invisible.

#### How can B2B brands win visibility in zero-click search?

B2B brands can improve zero-click visibility by answering specific buying questions with concise explanations, verifiable evidence, and clear entity facts. Map each decision to a useful page, keep that page accessible, and monitor citations separately from visits. Give qualified visitors a relevant diagnostic or service scope when they need deeper evaluation.

### What the 60% zero-click search headline actually means

The headline rounds a historical finding: SparkToro and Datos reported that 58.5% of US and 59.7% of EU Google searches in their 2024 panel ended without a result click. These are regional, browser-based observations, not a current universal rate or a B2B-only benchmark. The [original study and its limitations](https://sparktoro.com/blog/2024-zero-click-search-study-for-every-1000-us-google-searches-only-374-clicks-go-to-the-open-web-in-the-eu-its-360/) matter more than the rounded headline.

A search can end because the answer was sufficient, the buyer changed the question, or the session stopped. None of those events proves a commercial loss. For a B2B agency or software company, the practical problem is narrower: useful demand may exist where a traffic report cannot observe it. Design your content and reporting to distinguish influence, evidence, and visits instead of assigning the same value to every impression.


### Separate the answer, the citation, and the recommendation

An answer can use a source without recommending the business that published it. A citation can point to a research article while the shortlist names other vendors. A recommendation can name your company without providing a link. These outcomes need separate fields in your measurement log because they imply different next actions.

Suppose a buyer asks how to evaluate a customer onboarding platform. Your implementation guide is cited, but your product is absent from the vendor comparison. The guide may be doing useful educational work; the commercial gap may sit on your integration or suitability pages. Rewriting the successful guide into a sales pitch could weaken the asset that already helps the buyer. Diagnose which decision remains unsupported before changing it.

- Answer coverage: does the page resolve the actual question?
- Citation coverage: does the observed answer link to your evidence?
- Recommendation coverage: is your brand included for a relevant use case?
- Conversion coverage: is there a useful next step for the visitor who arrives?


### Build an answer-to-evidence map for commercial questions

Choose one offer and write ten questions a qualified buyer would ask before a call. Include suitability, alternatives, implementation, budget, and risk. Assign one primary URL to each decision. Then record the specific evidence that page needs: supported integrations, a transparent scope, a dated methodology, or a worked example.

Use a simple planning score: commercial relevance from one to three, evidence readiness from one to three, and implementation effort from one to three. Multiply relevance by readiness and divide by effort to order the first queue. This is Aeoba's suggested prioritization tool, not a ranking formula. It helps a team choose a useful comparison page ahead of a broad awareness article that has no evidence or commercial owner.

#### A worked B2B example

For an integration consultancy, replace a vague target such as ‘cloud expertise’ with ‘What should a mid-market finance team check before migrating its reporting stack?’ The answer page should explain prerequisites, delivery stages, data risks, and acceptance criteria. Link to the relevant service scope. Even if a summary satisfies the initial question, the page gives a serious evaluator a reason to return for the implementation detail.


### Make each answer useful outside its original page

Open a section with a direct answer that names the subject and its limits. Follow with evidence, a comparison, and an example. A paragraph saying ‘it depends on your situation’ becomes more useful when it specifies which situation: regulated data, a small delivery team, a multi-region rollout, or a restricted budget.

Keep important facts in readable page text. Add descriptive headings, stable URLs, and contextual internal links. Review technical access before inventing a special AI publishing format: [Google's AI-feature guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) does not require special AI schema. Our recommendation is to make the answer complete enough to stand on its own and detailed enough to reward a visit.


### Give the remaining click a commercial purpose

A visitor who already understands the category needs help making a decision. Send that visitor to a concrete diagnostic, scope, integration reference, or example. Repeating the article introduction behind a form adds friction without supplying new value. Explain what a report will examine and what information you need to prepare it.

For this topic, the natural next step is to inspect whether your own commercial pages support the buyer questions you want to appear for. Start with the [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report), or review [Managed AEO + SEO](https://aeoba.com/services/managed-aeo) for an execution program. Connect the article to the service that can resolve the identified problem, using anchor text that tells the reader what comes next.


### Measure zero-click influence without inventing attribution

Maintain a stable prompt panel and save the engine, date, answer, and source URLs. Review referral sessions and qualified enquiries separately. Add a short ‘How did you first hear about us?’ question to your commercial process and retain the buyer's wording. A self-reported AI discovery is useful evidence, but it is still different from a measured click path.

Illustrative example: a panel contains twenty prompts, checked twice each. Six of forty answers cite your domain. That is 15% observed citation coverage for those checks, not 15% of the market. If one later enquiry mentions ChatGPT, record it alongside the sales evidence without declaring the six citations responsible. For the reporting template, read [how to track AI visibility](https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/track-ai-search-visibility-attribution).

- Week one: choose the offer, prompt panel, and baseline conditions.
- Week two: repair the highest-value answer and its evidence gaps.
- Week three: connect supporting pages, service scope, and report CTA.
- Week four: repeat the checks and decide which gap deserves the next release.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### Does zero-click search mean SEO is no longer valuable?

No. Discoverable, useful commercial pages still capture demand and provide evidence. Add answer and citation observations to traffic reporting so your program can evaluate more of the buyer journey.

##### Can a B2B brand guarantee an AI citation?

A brand controls its publishing and technical access, but not an engine's source selection. Use a documented prompt panel and repeated observations to assess progress rather than treating a single citation as a permanent position.

##### What should we optimize first?

Start with one valuable buyer decision and its primary page. Check access, factual completeness, proof, internal links, and the next step before commissioning a larger content calendar.

### Why ChatGPT Recommends Your Competitor Instead of You (And How to Fix It in 90 Days)

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/rank-in-chatgpt-90-day-brand-visibility

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-23
Updated: 2026-11-23

A buyer asks ChatGPT for three suppliers. Your competitor appears with a specific reason to buy; your company disappears despite having a better product. The useful question is which part of your buyer-fit evidence is missing, inaccessible, or contradicted.

#### How can a business improve its visibility in ChatGPT?

Improve ChatGPT visibility by identifying the buyer questions where the brand is missing, checking search access, and publishing accurate evidence about fit, implementation, and limitations. Reconcile public business facts and relevant external references, then repeat documented checks. A ninety-day program provides an execution cycle rather than a universal recommendation deadline.

### There is no single ChatGPT ranking to fix

‘How to rank in ChatGPT’ is a useful commercial search, but it can suggest a fixed results page that does not exist. Recommendations vary with the prompt, conversation, search use, and available context. A generic ‘best platforms’ answer and a detailed ‘best platforms for a European finance team using this CRM’ answer are different evaluations.

Start with the exact questions your buyers ask, then record the observed answer and sources. Separate responses that used web search from those that did not. Treat your diagnosis as a set of hypotheses: the brand may be hard to identify, the relevant capability may be absent from public pages, or the cited comparisons may simply omit it. None of these explanations can be established from one disappointing screenshot.


### Diagnose five reasons your competitor has stronger evidence

Compare the evidence presented in the actual answer. If the competitor is described as an ideal fit for a specific integration, inspect the cited integration page. If it is recommended for a market or team size, find the public facts that support that description. Record what is explicit and what is only your interpretation.

Do the same exercise for your company without assuming that a polished homepage resolves every buyer concern. A feature may exist but lack public documentation. An old directory profile may still describe an earlier product. A service page may say ‘global expertise’ without naming the scope or delivery constraints. Fix the smallest factual gap that would help a human evaluate the same decision.

- Identity gap: inconsistent company names, domains, or service descriptions.
- Fit gap: no public explanation of the use case in the prompt.
- Proof gap: claims lack inspectable examples, documentation, or methodology.
- Access gap: important pages are blocked, unavailable, or require sign-in.
- Reference gap: relevant third-party sources omit or misdescribe the offer.


### Days 1–15: establish access and a reproducible baseline

Choose fifteen to thirty high-intent prompts and label them by audience, market, and buying stage. Run each under documented conditions more than once. Store the wording, date, product or mode, mention, recommendation, cited URL, and any retrieval failure. Make a separate list for new exploratory prompts so your original comparison set stays stable.

Check robots rules and your delivery infrastructure. [OpenAI distinguishes OAI-SearchBot from GPTBot](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots): search discovery and model-training controls serve different purposes. Review the current guidance and verify actual access in your logs rather than relying on the name of a robots rule. An allowed crawler still does not guarantee a recommendation. Keep the technical audit connected to the pages the prompt panel actually needs.

#### Create a useful baseline record

A record might read: procurement lead; EU market; comparison stage; exact prompt; search-enabled response; company not mentioned; two competitor URLs cited; checked on a stated date. Add a screenshot or answer export where available. A missing result caused by an error should be marked unobserved, not counted as a competitive loss.


### Days 16–45: publish the missing buying evidence

Build a small set of pages that explain suitability, implementation, integrations, and alternatives. Each should own a specific decision and make its claims testable. A comparison needs explicit criteria, relevant tradeoffs, and a review date. An implementation guide needs prerequisites, stages, responsibilities, and limits. Avoid producing several pages that repeat the same broad category pitch.

For a B2B SaaS company, start with a use-case page and the integration detail that sales repeatedly sends by email. For a service agency, document who the engagement fits, what the first month contains, and what the client must supply. Connect these pages to the main offer and supporting guides. [Technical AEO](https://aeoba.com/services/technical-aeo) helps align their entities and markup; it cannot replace the underlying proof.


### Days 46–75: repair external facts and earn relevant coverage

Prioritize sources already appearing in your observed answers. Check whether those sources cover the right market and whether your company belongs in their editorial scope. Request corrections to inaccurate factual profiles through the publisher's normal process. For new coverage, contribute useful research, implementation lessons, or a practical comparison resource that gives the editor a reason to consider the material.

Keep editorial outreach separate from purchased distribution. A paid article can provide information, but it should not be presented as an independent endorsement. Disclose commercial relationships and respect community rules. The useful operating goal is a more accurate public evidence base, supported by dated URLs. Whether an engine later cites a source remains a separate observation. Aeoba's [authority and community work](https://aeoba.com/services/authority-community-mentions) follows that distinction.


### Days 76–90: evaluate progress and choose the next experiment

Repeat the original panel and compare mention coverage, relevant recommendations, owned citations, and third-party citations. Retain the raw counts and denominator. Look at which buyer decisions improved and whether the observed answer now describes the offer accurately. Do not combine an expanded prompt set with the original baseline and call the difference growth.

Ninety days is a planning window for diagnosis, implementation, and review; it is not a universal time-to-rank promise. If access is fixed but recommendations remain absent, inspect the source gap. If citations rise but enquiries do not, review fit and the destination experience. Start with the [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report), then use [AI Visibility Recovery](https://aeoba.com/services/ai-visibility-recovery) when you need a focused investigation rather than an undirected publishing sprint.

- Ship log: what changed, where, and when?
- Visibility log: what did the same checks actually show?
- Commercial log: which visits or enquiries have supporting attribution?
- Next experiment: which unresolved gap has the strongest evidence?


#### Frequently asked questions

##### Can I pay OpenAI to rank my company in ChatGPT answers?

This playbook concerns organic visibility and public evidence. Advertising or other commercial products should not be treated as a way to guarantee an organic recommendation or citation.

##### Will allowing GPTBot make ChatGPT recommend us?

No. GPTBot and the search crawler have different documented roles. Review search access separately and evaluate whether the public pages answer the buyer's question; crawler access alone establishes no recommendation guarantee.

##### What can a small team accomplish in 90 days?

A small team can establish a defensible baseline, repair important access and identity gaps, ship a focused group of buyer-fit pages, and evaluate repeat checks. Scope the plan around evidence and delivery capacity.

### AEO vs. GEO vs. Traditional SEO: What Actually Moves Pipeline in 2026

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/aeo-vs-geo-vs-seo-pipeline-2026

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-23
Updated: 2026-11-23

Three agencies can sell you SEO, AEO, and GEO while proposing the same technical fixes and content pages. The label is cheap. The valuable distinction is which buyer decision the work supports and which outcome the team can prove.

#### What is the difference between AEO, GEO, and SEO?

SEO supports discovery and useful presentation in search results. AEO emphasizes clear answers and supporting evidence, while GEO examines representation in generated responses. Their technical and editorial work overlaps. A B2B program should prioritize the buyer decision and observed constraint, then report citations, visits, qualified pipeline, and revenue separately.

### Define SEO, AEO, and GEO before comparing them

SEO focuses on discovery and useful presentation in search engines. AEO, Answer Engine Optimization, focuses on making information usable in direct answers and supported recommendations. GEO, Generative Engine Optimization, describes work intended to improve representation in generated responses. These are working industry terms with overlapping usage, not three universally standardized products.

Aeoba uses the distinctions to clarify a scope. Technical access and canonicalization can support all three. A direct answer with evidence is useful in both a traditional result and an AI summary. A prompt-and-citation panel adds observations that a conventional keyword report may not contain. A proposal should explain these deliverables directly so the buyer can compare substance rather than count acronyms.

| Discipline | Primary question | Useful evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SEO | Can buyers discover and use the page through search? | Indexation, relevant search performance, visits, conversions |
| AEO | Can an answer resolve the question and cite supporting facts? | Answer quality, observed mentions and source URLs |
| GEO | How is the brand represented in generated responses? | Repeated response samples, accuracy, fit, citations |


### Follow one buying journey across all three disciplines

Imagine an operations director selecting compliance software. The first search asks about implementation risks. A later prompt compares suppliers that meet a regional requirement. A colleague checks integrations in a conventional search result. The final website visit lands on pricing. Assigning the entire opportunity to one channel discards the evidence from the other steps.

Build one decision map covering research, evaluation, validation, and purchase. Use it to identify the page, evidence, and next step for each stage. An implementation guide may support early confidence. An integration reference may resolve a blocker. A comparison may narrow the shortlist. The program moves toward pipeline when those assets help qualified buyers advance, even when not every earlier interaction leaves a measurable click.


### Keep the technical foundation shared

Do not buy three separate audits of the same canonical URLs, crawl rules, rendering, and internal links. Create one technical backlog with clear acceptance criteria. A commercial page should return successfully, be reachable through descriptive links, represent the correct entity, and make its important content available to visitors.

Assign one owner to each shared fix and record which page templates it affects. This prevents multiple providers from making conflicting changes to the same metadata or organization record. A coordinated release also gives the measurement team a reliable date to use when investigating later observations.

[Google's guidance on AI features](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) keeps foundational SEO relevant and introduces no special AI-feature technical requirements. Treat claims of a separate mandatory AI markup layer cautiously. A practical audit should identify the page, the observed defect, the proposed repair, and the validation method. [Technical AEO](https://aeoba.com/services/technical-aeo) connects that work to consistent brand and service facts.

#### Define completion before implementation

‘Improve entity optimization’ is difficult to review. ‘Use one organization identifier, reconcile the contact details across visible pages and JSON-LD, and remove duplicate conflicting records’ is concrete. Agree on the observable output before the work starts, then keep the release record with the prompt or page it was intended to support.


### Allocate content by commercial friction

Start with the questions that block a real purchase. Interview sales and delivery teams, review anonymized objections, and inspect the material buyers request before signing. A missing integration page or ambiguous service scope may deserve attention before another broad explainer. Create an evidence brief before a writing brief so every important claim has a source or a documented gap.

Use an illustrative capacity split such as half the effort on commercial-page gaps, a quarter on technical repairs, and a quarter on measurement and relevant external evidence. This is a planning example, not an industry benchmark. Change it when the audit shows a different bottleneck. An inaccessible site needs technical work first; a healthy site with weak differentiation needs better facts and explanations.

- High buying intent + clear evidence: improve the primary commercial page.
- High buying intent + weak evidence: commission the research or documentation.
- Strong content + poor access: resolve the technical constraint.
- Frequent citations + weak enquiries: inspect audience fit and conversion friction.


### Use a pipeline model with visible assumptions

A simple commercial model starts with qualified visits, enquiry rate, qualification rate, average opportunity value, and win rate. Keep pipeline separate from revenue. For example, 100 visits producing five enquiries and two qualified opportunities at €20,000 each imply €40,000 of opportunity pipeline. At a stated 25% win assumption, the model suggests €10,000 of potential revenue. These are illustrative inputs, not Aeoba results.

A citation is upstream evidence, not a visit and not an opportunity. Report observed citation coverage beside referral sessions and buyer-reported discovery, then show the commercial outcomes that actually occurred. If a buyer mentions an AI answer after arriving through branded search, retain both observations. [AI Search Analytics](https://aeoba.com/services/ai-search-analytics) can build that reporting discipline without pretending to recover every unseen interaction.


### Choose a program by outputs and review cadence

Ask the provider to show the baseline, the first execution queue, the evidence requirements, and the weekly review. The agreement should name who approves claims, who implements technical changes, and how results are checked. A proposal selling a content count without a decision map makes it difficult to know whether the work addresses a commercial constraint.

Start with a [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report) if the bottleneck is unclear. Use [Managed AEO + SEO](https://aeoba.com/services/managed-aeo) when the work needs coordinated technical, content, authority, and measurement execution. Then assess the first ninety days against shipped improvements and documented buyer outcomes. The acronym matters less than the team's ability to connect a question, a page, supporting facts, and an accountable next action.

- One prompt and page map for the offer.
- One technical backlog with observable acceptance criteria.
- One editorial queue grounded in inspectable evidence.
- Separate reporting for discovery, citations, qualified opportunities, and revenue.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### What is the main difference between AEO and GEO?

AEO emphasizes answering questions clearly and supporting answers with evidence. GEO emphasizes representation in generative responses. The terms overlap, so compare the actual work and measurement definitions in a proposal.

##### Does GEO replace traditional SEO in 2026?

No. Technical discovery, useful content, and a clear conversion experience remain part of the same buyer journey. Add generative-response observations where relevant rather than abandoning the foundation.

##### Which discipline should a B2B company fund first?

Fund the most important observed constraint. Fix blocked commercial pages before scaling content; improve weak buying evidence before expanding a prompt dashboard. A shared diagnostic is more useful than selecting a label in isolation.

### The Exact Schema & Entity Blueprint LLMs Use to Verify Your Brand

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/technical-aeo-schema-entity-blueprint

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-23
Updated: 2026-11-23

If your footer names one business, your schema names another, and your service pages imply a third, adding more JSON-LD creates a larger contradiction. Start with one verifiable account of the brand before adding another property.

#### Which schema and entity work should a brand implement first?

Start with a canonical brand fact sheet and an accurate Organization record linked to the services and pages it describes. Use stable identifiers, current contact details, and visible location facts. Validate syntax, vocabulary, and factual agreement separately. No public schema blueprint guarantees verification or recommendations across all language models.

### What an entity blueprint can actually establish

No public specification reveals an exact verification pipeline shared by every LLM. The blueprint here is an implementable approach to consistent brand facts, not a claim to know a model's private ranking logic. Its purpose is to make the organization, services, locations, and evidence understandable in both visible pages and machine-readable descriptions.

[Google's Organization documentation](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/organization) explains how organization markup can help disambiguate a business. That is a narrower and more useful claim than saying schema guarantees an AI recommendation. Treat factual consistency as the deliverable you control; record actual citations and brand descriptions separately when evaluating the result.


### Step 1: create a canonical brand fact sheet

List the public brand name, canonical domain, logo URL, contact email, operating locations, service names, and confirmed profile URLs. Beside each field, identify the page where a visitor can verify it and the team responsible for keeping it current. A shared source of truth is especially useful when several templates render contact details independently.

For Aeoba, that public identity is the agency brand, info@aeoba.com, Milan in Italy, and Sliema in Malta. Do not invent a street address, a legal designation, or a review score to make the record look more complete. Keep operating locations separate from claims about a staffed storefront. The evidence should determine the model, rather than a schema generator determining what the business claims to be.

- Resolve conflicting names and legacy domains.
- Use current, public contact details in pages and markup.
- Describe real services with a clear scope and audience.
- Include only profiles that actually identify the organization.
- Assign a review owner and a change trigger for every important fact.


### Step 2: connect entities with stable identifiers

Use a durable organization identifier such as `https://aeoba.com/#organization` and reference it from related records. Give a service a distinct identifier, then connect it to the organization through `provider`. A page URL identifies a document; the organization identifier identifies the business. Keeping those roles separate prevents an article, a service, and a company from becoming interchangeable records.

The following compact example is an entity map, not a universal template. Adapt it to facts visible on the relevant pages. [Schema.org's Service type](https://schema.org/Service) supports describing a service and its provider. Additional properties are useful only when they express accurate information that helps someone understand the offer.

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@graph": [
    {
      "@type": "Organization",
      "@id": "https://aeoba.com/#organization",
      "name": "Aeoba",
      "url": "https://aeoba.com",
      "email": "info@aeoba.com",
      "location": [
        { "@type": "Place", "name": "Milan, Italy" },
        { "@type": "Place", "name": "Sliema, Malta" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "@type": "Service",
      "@id": "https://aeoba.com/services/technical-aeo#service",
      "name": "Technical AEO (Schema + Entity)",
      "url": "https://aeoba.com/services/technical-aeo",
      "provider": { "@id": "https://aeoba.com/#organization" }
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Avoid template-generated identity drift

Check what the final page emits when a CMS plugin, theme, and custom component all add organization records. Multiple records are not automatically wrong, but conflicting names or IDs create an avoidable maintenance problem. Keep one authoritative configuration and make intentional references to it from page-specific markup.


### Step 3: choose page-specific schema that matches the page

A service page should describe the service it actually offers. An editorial page can use `BlogPosting` and identify its headline, publication date, author, publisher, and canonical page. [Google's article guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/article) covers article properties and author identification. A brand publication can identify an organization as its author when that matches the visible byline.

Keep a FAQ visible if you describe it in markup. Do not add a hidden catalogue of questions solely for a crawler. A valid schema vocabulary does not mean a page qualifies for every search appearance, and an ordinary agency blog should not promise FAQ rich results. Choose the smallest accurate representation first, then review the relevant engine's eligibility guidance before expanding it.


### Step 4: validate access, syntax, meaning, and deployment

Validation needs several checks. Fetch the actual public URL and inspect the delivered HTML. Parse every JSON-LD script to catch syntax failures. Use a vocabulary validator to review types and properties. Compare names, services, dates, locations, and claims with visible content. These checks answer different questions; passing a parser does not establish factual accuracy.

Include a changed-page check in the release process. If an editor updates a service name, confirm that the navigation label, visible heading, structured record, and relevant internal links still identify the same offer. Store a short validation note with the release so another team member can distinguish an approved fact change from accidental template drift.

After deployment, inspect more than the homepage. A shared component can be correct while a page template emits an older record. Check representative service, article, contact, and location pages. Verify canonical URLs and internal links, then retain a short release record showing what changed and what was checked. [Technical AEO](https://aeoba.com/services/technical-aeo) should produce reviewable corrections rather than an unexplained schema score.

- Access: can the intended public page be retrieved successfully?
- Syntax: does every JSON-LD block parse?
- Vocabulary: do the chosen types and properties express the intended facts?
- Meaning: does markup agree with the visible page?
- Release: does the production output contain the approved implementation?


### Step 5: maintain the graph when business facts change

Put identity review into ordinary publishing work. A new service, revised contact email, changed location, or updated article should trigger the corresponding visible-page and markup checks. Store shared facts in configuration and page-specific facts beside their content so maintenance follows the same editorial process.

Then evaluate the commercial question: are observed AI descriptions more accurate, are relevant pages cited, and can buyers understand the offer? Those observations do not prove that schema alone caused a change, but they reveal whether the combined system is becoming more useful. Request the [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report) to identify the first gaps, or read the [90-day implementation playbook](https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/90-day-answer-engine-playbook-b2b) to connect technical cleanup with content and measurement.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### Is there a special schema type required for LLM visibility?

There is no universal LLM-visibility schema standard. Use accurate, established types for the organization and page, and verify the requirements of the specific search feature you are targeting.

##### Should an agency use Organization or LocalBusiness?

Choose the type that accurately represents the business and the page. Do not imply a storefront, street address, or local operating model that you cannot substantiate. Organization is a useful starting point for the agency identity.

##### Will valid JSON-LD guarantee ChatGPT or Perplexity citations?

No. Valid, consistent markup is an implementation quality measure. Source selection and recommendations need separate observation, and the page must still provide useful evidence for the buyer's question.

### Why Reddit and 'Best Of' Listicles Matter More Than Backlinks for Perplexity Rankings

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/perplexity-seo-reddit-listicles-citation-signals

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-23
Updated: 2026-11-23

A competitor earns one detailed comparison mention while you earn twenty irrelevant links. If the buyer asks which supplier fits a particular workflow, the comparison may contain the evidence the answer needs. A link-count report cannot tell you that.

#### How should a business approach Perplexity SEO?

Approach Perplexity SEO by inspecting the sources returned for specific buyer questions, improving accessible primary evidence, and earning relevant editorial or community references. A useful discussion or comparison may support a decision better than unrelated links. Treat that as a source-relevance hypothesis and verify citations through repeated observations.

### Treat the headline as a source-relevance hypothesis

There is no published universal Perplexity formula proving that Reddit or listicles always outweigh backlinks. The practical argument is conditional: when those sources answer your buyer's question and appear in the observed response, improving relevant coverage can deserve more attention than increasing an unrelated backlink total.

This is a research priority, not a ranking guarantee. Begin with the exact prompt and sources the engine actually returns. A specialist documentation page may matter more than either a community thread or a comparison article. Your task is to identify the evidence required by the decision, then build a legitimate contribution that belongs in that context. Do not turn a useful editorial tactic into a claim about secret algorithm weights.

Agree on the experiment's question before outreach begins. For example: does a clearer public integration guide give relevant editors better material to evaluate? That question creates an inspectable output even if the next engine check does not change. It also separates editorial progress from an unverified assumption about rankings.

- Find the decision and its observed sources.
- Verify the factual gap before proposing a contribution.
- Publish useful primary evidence and disclose relationships.
- Repeat the panel and record what the answer actually cites.


### Inspect the sources behind high-intent Perplexity answers

Choose a small panel of comparison, suitability, implementation, and risk questions. Run repeat checks and save each source URL, the claim it supports, the publication date if visible, and whether it describes your market. Separate owned product pages, independent editorial coverage, communities, directories, and paid placements.

Use this log to look for patterns rather than declaring a platform preference from one answer. If several relevant questions cite detailed integration documentation, your first priority may be your own documentation. If a recurring comparison excludes your category, inspect the criteria before pitching inclusion. A source opportunity is valuable when it can help the evaluator understand a real difference, not simply because it already appears in an answer.

| Source | What to inspect | Useful response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Community discussion | Specific problem, firsthand detail, moderation rules | Answer the problem with disclosed expertise |
| Best-of comparison | Criteria, audience, update policy, relationships | Offer verifiable facts relevant to the criteria |
| Product documentation | Capability, prerequisites, limitations | Publish missing implementation detail |
| Directory profile | Identity and service accuracy | Correct outdated business facts |


### Why a useful Reddit answer can support buyer evaluation

A discussion can surface the exact objections polished marketing copy omits: setup friction, a missing integration, procurement concerns, or a workflow that fails at a certain scale. Those details can help a buyer evaluate suitability. The value comes from specificity and a transparent context, not from the Reddit domain by itself.

Research each community before participating. Read its rules, check whether commercial relationships must be disclosed, and contribute only where you can answer the question. An explanation should remain useful without a link. Never manufacture a satisfied customer, coordinate votes, or plant an undisclosed endorsement. These practices damage the evidence base you are trying to improve and can make the underlying contribution less credible to the people who matter.

#### A contribution that stands on its own

For an implementation question, explain the prerequisites, the main tradeoff, and the failure case. State your relationship to the product or service. If a public resource adds necessary detail and the rules allow it, link directly to that resource. Keep a record of the contribution and its context; measure an actual AI citation only if a later check observes one.


### Earn comparison coverage with an evidence packet

An editor evaluating ‘best software for distributed finance teams’ needs accurate facts: supported markets, integrations, implementation requirements, pricing availability, and constraints. Prepare a compact packet with source URLs and a clear explanation of where the product fits. Include the limitations that a serious buyer would need to know.

Read the publication's methodology and disclosure policy. Suggest a correction or a candidate for review through its editorial process. If the only route is a paid placement, label and track it as paid distribution. Avoid publishing a supposedly independent ‘best providers’ list that silently ranks your own company first. Aeoba's [authority and community services](https://aeoba.com/services/authority-community-mentions) focus on useful references with a clear relationship to the brand.


### Keep your own pages accessible and worth citing

Third-party work cannot compensate for unclear or unavailable primary information. Provide a stable destination where a buyer can verify the capability, scope, and contact details referenced elsewhere. Keep your comparison and implementation pages current, and connect them through meaningful internal links.

[Perplexity's crawler documentation](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/resources/perplexity-crawlers) distinguishes its search crawler from user-initiated fetches and describes access configuration. Verify applicable crawler and infrastructure rules using the current documentation. Access is a prerequisite you can inspect; it is not evidence of a particular ranking. [Technical AEO](https://aeoba.com/services/technical-aeo) can resolve the owned-site gaps while your editorial program develops relevant external references.


### Run a four-week source experiment

In week one, establish the prompt panel and classify its citations. In week two, improve one primary evidence page and prepare a factual editorial packet. In week three, pursue a small number of appropriate corrections or contributions. In week four, repeat the checks and inspect what changed. External editors control their publishing schedules, so a four-week experiment may end with useful submissions rather than published coverage.

Record inputs, outputs, and observations separately: contributions prepared, pieces accepted, source URLs published, citations observed, and enquiries received. Do not describe every acquired link as an AI visibility win. Start with the [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report), then compare your source findings with the [ChatGPT visibility plan](https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/rank-in-chatgpt-90-day-brand-visibility) to identify work that supports more than one engine.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### Does Perplexity always favor Reddit?

No universal preference is established here. Inspect the sources returned for your own high-intent prompts and repeat the checks. Source usefulness depends on the question and the evidence available.

##### Are backlinks irrelevant to Perplexity SEO?

No. Relevant links can help people discover useful information and can accompany strong editorial evidence. A backlink count alone does not tell you whether a source supports the buyer's decision or is cited in an observed answer.

##### Should we buy placements in best-of articles?

Evaluate the audience, editorial process, factual usefulness, and disclosure first. Paid distribution should be recorded as paid and cannot establish an independent endorsement or guarantee a citation.

### How to Track AI Search Visibility When Google Search Console Shows Zero Clicks

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/track-ai-search-visibility-attribution

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-23
Updated: 2026-11-23

An AI answer can name your company and cite your research while Search Console records no click. That is not automatically a tracking failure. It is a reminder that a citation, a visit, and a sales opportunity are three different events.

#### How do you track AI visibility without referral clicks?

Track AI visibility through dated prompt observations that distinguish mentions, recommendations, and cited sources. Use analytics for visits with available attribution and commercial records for qualified opportunities. Combine these with buyer-reported discovery while preserving their different certainty levels. Google Search Console alone does not measure citations across other answer engines.

### Start with the boundary of each measurement system

Search Console reports Google Search performance; it is not a cross-engine monitor for ChatGPT and Perplexity. [Google documents AI-feature traffic within its Web performance reporting](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features). A zero-click row therefore cannot prove that another engine omitted your brand, nor can a citation screenshot prove that a user visited your site.

Build a measurement stack that preserves those boundaries. Use prompt observations for what an answer said, web analytics for recorded visits, and your commercial system for qualified opportunities. Connect records when evidence supports the connection. Retain uncertainty when a buyer's path crosses devices, applications, untagged links, or a later branded search. A useful report should make that uncertainty visible instead of hiding it in a single score.


### Define four metrics before selecting a dashboard

A brand mention means the answer explicitly names the company. A citation means the answer includes an inspectable source reference. An owned-domain citation and a third-party source discussing your brand should be separate categories. A qualified opportunity requires your business's qualification criteria, not merely a form submission.

Define recommendation accuracy as well: a brand named for a capability it does not provide is not a useful win. Save whether the description matches the offer and whether the recommendation addresses the prompt. These fields make a small manual log more actionable than a large volume of unlabeled screenshots. Publish your definitions beside the report so stakeholders know what a change in coverage actually means.

| Metric | Suggested calculation | What it cannot establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mention coverage | Checks naming the brand / completed checks | Market share or a click |
| Owned citation coverage | Checks citing the domain / completed checks | A visit or a recommendation |
| Observed AI referrals | Sessions with supporting source evidence | All AI-influenced visits |
| Qualified pipeline | Value of qualified opportunities under agreed criteria | Revenue already won |


### Build a stable, commercially relevant prompt panel

Use sales and delivery questions to choose prompts across discovery, comparison, suitability, implementation, and risk. Add the audience and market when they affect the answer. Keep exact wording stable within a reporting period. If you introduce a new product or category, create a new cohort rather than rewriting the baseline without explanation.

Run repeated checks under documented conditions. Save the engine or product, available mode, search use, date, region where relevant, prompt, answer excerpt, source URLs, and result status. Distinguish a technical failure from a completed answer with no mention. Automated API checks and consumer-interface checks may represent different experiences; label them separately instead of merging them into a single time series.

#### A denominator example

Suppose twenty-five prompts are checked twice. Two checks fail, leaving forty-eight completed observations. Twelve cite your domain, giving 25% observed owned citation coverage for that panel. Report the two failed checks as missing. If the next period has more failures or different prompts, explain the comparison limit before interpreting the change.


### Capture available referral and conversion evidence

Inspect source and medium, the available referrer, campaign parameters, landing page, and conversion events in your analytics setup. Validate a controlled visit from the actual interface before relying on a channel grouping. Different clients can preserve different information, and a redirected or copied link can lose source context. Treat a missing referrer as unknown rather than automatically assigning it to AI.

Attach the recorded first landing page and attribution details to an enquiry when your implementation and privacy choices allow it. Add a concise discovery question to the sales process. A buyer saying ‘I compared you in ChatGPT’ is useful self-reported influence. Keep it separate from a technically observed referral so your team can evaluate both without double-counting the opportunity.

- Test the source evidence with an actual controlled visit.
- Separate detected referrals from self-reported discovery.
- Keep direct and branded traffic available for investigation.
- Deduplicate enquiries and opportunities using your commercial process.
- Document consent, retention, and access practices for the data you collect.


### Connect the visibility report to shipped work

Maintain a change log containing the release date, page, prompt cohort, and intended effect. A schema correction may target entity accuracy. An integration guide may target implementation questions. An editorial contribution may create a new independent source. Review whether the next observations are consistent with the intended effect without assuming that sequence alone proves causation.

Keep raw exports available to the reviewer rather than retaining only a chart. If a classification changes, preserve the original observation and explain the correction. This allows a team to revise its definitions without silently rewriting the historical trend it uses for commercial decisions.

Investigate lost coverage using the saved source record. Did the cited page change, become inaccessible, or move? Did a source update its comparison? Did your checks change product or mode? These questions often produce a more useful repair than rewriting the homepage after every fluctuation. [AI Search Analytics](https://aeoba.com/services/ai-search-analytics) and the [Answer Index](https://aeoba.com/answer-index) support this evidence-first review process.


### Make the weekly report end in a decision

A useful weekly report can fit on one page: completed checks and exceptions, mention and citation coverage, important answer examples, shipped changes, recorded referrals, qualified opportunities, and the next three actions. Include source URLs or answer exports so another person can inspect the basis for the recommendation.

If coverage improves without relevant enquiries, review audience fit and the conversion destination. If enquiries improve while citations remain flat, inspect other sources of demand before crediting the program. If the evidence is too sparse, improve the sampling or instrumentation. Start with a [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report), then use the [AEO, GEO, and SEO comparison](https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/aeo-vs-geo-vs-seo-pipeline-2026) to connect these metrics to a coordinated commercial program.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### Does Search Console show ChatGPT citations?

Search Console covers Google Search performance. Use separate observed-answer records for ChatGPT citations and your analytics system for visits with available referral evidence.

##### What is a good AI citation coverage percentage?

There is no universal target that applies to every market or prompt set. Establish a stable panel tied to commercial decisions, report completed observations, and compare progress using the same definitions and conditions.

##### Can we attribute every AI-influenced deal?

No. Some influence leaves no measurable click path. Combine detected referral evidence, buyer-reported discovery, and qualified opportunity records while preserving their different levels of certainty.

### The 90-Day Answer Engine Playbook for B2B SaaS and Service Companies

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/90-day-answer-engine-playbook-b2b

Author: Aeoba
Published: 2026-11-23
Updated: 2026-11-23

A ninety-day AEO program can ship dozens of articles and still leave the sales team's hardest question unanswered. Start with the decision that stalls a purchase, then build the technical access, content, and evidence needed to resolve it.

#### What belongs in a 90-day B2B AEO plan?

A ninety-day B2B AEO plan should define the offer and buyer questions, establish a citation baseline, repair technical and entity gaps, publish evidence-led answers, and develop relevant external references. Repeat the original checks, inspect commercial outcomes, and choose the next constraint from the evidence rather than using article volume as the objective.

### Set the commercial scope before the content calendar

Choose one offer, one primary audience, and one market for the initial cycle. Define a qualified opportunity using criteria your sales team already understands. List the decisions a buyer must make before contacting you and the evidence required for each. Then name the people or functions responsible for strategy, technical changes, editorial review, and measurement.

A useful initial scope might be a prompt panel, a small cluster of commercial pages, a technical repair queue, an entity fact sheet, and a source log. The exact count should follow capacity and evidence readiness. Ninety days is an implementation and learning cycle, not a promise that every engine will recommend every brand on a fixed deadline.

| Phase | Main output | Exit check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Days 1–15 | Decision map, prompt baseline, access audit | The team can explain the offer and inspect the baseline |
| Days 16–30 | Technical repairs and consistent entity facts | Priority pages are accessible and factually aligned |
| Days 31–60 | Evidence-led answer and commercial pages | Each page resolves an assigned buyer decision |
| Days 61–75 | Relevant external corrections and contributions | Published sources and relationships are recorded accurately |
| Days 76–90 | Repeat checks and next-cycle roadmap | Decisions follow documented observations |


### Days 1–15: map buyer questions and record the baseline

Collect questions from sales calls, procurement requests, onboarding, and support. Group them by suitability, alternatives, implementation, cost, and risk. Keep the customer's wording where possible. Assign a primary page and evidence gap to each question, then choose a manageable subset for repeat engine checks.

For SaaS, include integration compatibility, migration effort, data handling, and team fit. For services, include deliverables, responsibilities, engagement scope, and handover. Record the exact prompt, engine or product, date, answer, and sources. A baseline is useful only if a later reviewer can reproduce its conditions well enough to understand the comparison. Use the [buyer-intent prompt guide](https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/build-a-buyer-intent-prompt-map) to structure the first map.

- Deliverable: agreed buyer-question and page map.
- Deliverable: dated observations with mentions and citations separated.
- Deliverable: a prioritized evidence and technical gap list.
- Review: confirm that the prompt panel represents actual buying decisions.


### Days 16–30: repair access and reconcile the brand

Inspect the primary commercial pages for response status, canonical URLs, discoverable links, readable content, and appropriate crawl access. Review the delivered HTML as well as the visible browser page. A blocked or contradictory page should be repaired before a content expansion sends more internal links toward it.

Create a brand fact sheet and align shared configuration, contact details, operating locations, and structured data. Keep an organization separate from its services and articles through stable identifiers. Record each repair with an acceptance check. The [schema and entity blueprint](https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/technical-aeo-schema-entity-blueprint) explains the implementation sequence; [Technical AEO](https://aeoba.com/services/technical-aeo) provides the corresponding service scope.

#### Keep the first release small enough to verify

Do not combine a redesign, a domain migration, and the initial answer program unless those projects are necessary to resolve the observed problem. Focused changes are easier to review and maintain. An initial release can contain a corrected entity configuration, a repaired service template, and a clearer implementation page, each with a documented purpose.


### Days 31–60: build pages around evidence, not volume

Write an evidence brief for each priority page. Include the question, direct answer, supporting facts, example, limitations, internal links, and next step. Put technical and commercial reviewers on the draft before publication. A comparison should disclose its criteria; a delivery guide should identify prerequisites and responsibilities; a case example should distinguish illustration from achieved client results.

Start with existing commercial pages when they already own the decision. Add a supporting article only when a separate information need justifies it. This avoids creating overlapping pages that compete for the same purpose. Link the supporting explanation to the service or product scope, then link back where it helps the buyer explore detail. [Managed AEO + SEO](https://aeoba.com/services/managed-aeo) coordinates this work around one execution queue.
