- SaaS example: use-case page, integration guide, migration checklist, and a criteria-led comparison.
- Service example: scope page, implementation timeline, responsibility matrix, and a qualification guide.
- Editorial check: every material claim has a source, evidence, or a clearly stated limitation.
- Conversion check: the next step gives the reader something useful for their current decision.


### Days 61–75: develop the public evidence beyond your site

Review the sources appearing in your baseline and identify legitimate opportunities to improve accuracy or contribute expertise. Correct outdated profiles, propose relevant editorial material, and participate in communities when the question and rules fit your expertise. Keep the contribution useful even if the publisher chooses not to link.

Prepare a source log with the URL, publication or update date, audience, relationship, and claim supported. Separate proposed work from published coverage. Keep paid distribution distinct from independent editorial references. An external mention becomes an observed AI citation only when an actual answer check includes it. The [Perplexity source strategy](https://aeoba.com/resources/blog/perplexity-seo-reddit-listicles-citation-signals) provides a practical research framework for this phase.


### Days 76–90: review results and commit to the next constraint

Repeat the original prompt panel under documented conditions and compare completed observations. Review brand accuracy, relevant recommendations, owned and third-party citations, available referral sessions, and qualified opportunities. Add the release log so stakeholders can see what shipped. Preserve uncertainty about causation and missing attribution.

Choose the next cycle from the evidence. If technical access remains weak, finish the repairs. If fit is poorly explained, improve the commercial pages. If the source landscape omits your category, invest in research and legitimate editorial contributions. If the program generates attention without qualified demand, reconsider the audience and offer. Request the [Free AEO Report](https://aeoba.com/free-aeo-report) to define a useful starting scope, or discuss [AI Search Analytics](https://aeoba.com/services/ai-search-analytics) when the measurement gap is preventing decisions.

#### A weekly review agenda that supports delivery

Review the work completed, the evidence checked, the blockers that need an owner, and the next three priorities. Keep approvals and due dates explicit. A short meeting with a visible delivery queue is more useful than a dashboard walkthrough that ends without a decision. Carry unresolved questions into the next cycle with a proposed way to investigate them.


#### Frequently asked questions

##### Is ninety days enough to see AEO results?

It is a useful period for establishing a baseline, shipping focused improvements, and reviewing repeated observations. Source updates, crawling, demand, and engine behavior vary, so it is not a universal deadline for recommendations or revenue.

##### How many articles should a B2B company publish?

Publish the number needed to resolve distinct buyer decisions with useful evidence and available review capacity. Improve existing commercial pages first when they already own the question. Content volume alone is not an implementation objective.

##### Can SaaS and service companies use the same playbook?

Yes, the sequence is shared: scope, baseline, access, evidence, references, and review. The underlying buying questions differ, so SaaS integration and migration evidence should not be substituted for a service company's scope and delivery responsibilities.

## Glossary

### Answer Engine Optimization

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/aeo

The work of making a brand's expertise understandable, useful, and supportable in answers generated by search and AI systems. A practical program connects buyer questions to accessible pages, consistent business entities, relevant proof, and repeat citation checks. Measure observed answers separately from website visits and qualified enquiries.

### Generative Engine Optimization

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/geo

A term for improving how a business and its content are represented in generated answers, including entity clarity, evidence, and source quality. Its scope overlaps with AEO and SEO. Use clear business facts and useful public sources, then evaluate actual answers under documented conditions rather than assuming a universal generative ranking formula.

### Search Engine Optimization

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/seo

Technical, content, and authority work that helps search engines discover, understand, and present useful pages. The foundation includes crawl access, canonical URLs, descriptive metadata, useful content, and contextual links. Evaluate qualified demand and commercial outcomes alongside search impressions and visits, with clear definitions for each observation.

### Entity

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/entity

A distinguishable person, organization, product, service, place, or concept with a consistent identity and relationships. Stable names, identifiers, and accurate public facts help distinguish one entity from another. In AEO, reconcile the agency, service, and location records before connecting them with structured data or publishing additional claims.

### AI citation

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/citation

An inspectable source reference included in an AI answer. A named mention without a source is recorded separately. Keep the answer excerpt, engine, exact prompt, date, and source URL together. A citation can support information without recommending its publisher, and it does not establish that a buyer clicked or became a customer.

### Buyer intent

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/buyer-intent

The decision or commercial need behind a question, such as comparing alternatives, checking suitability, or estimating implementation effort. Record who is asking, what decision they face, and which evidence would resolve it. Use this context to prioritize commercial pages and supporting answers instead of treating every keyword variation as a separate content opportunity.

### Structured data / schema

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/schema

Machine-readable descriptions of visible facts and relationships, often expressed as JSON-LD on a web page. Use accurate types and properties to connect the business with its services and publications. Validate syntax and meaning separately, keep markup synchronized with visible content, and avoid promising rich results or AI citations from validity alone.

### JSON-LD

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/json-ld

A JSON-based format for linked data used to describe entities and connect them with stable identifiers. On an agency website, it can describe an organization, its services, published articles, and visible questions. Escape script-breaking characters, reuse consistent identifiers, and check the final rendered output rather than trusting a template configuration alone.

### Canonical URL

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/canonical

The preferred URL declared for a page to help consolidate duplicate or overlapping versions. Use a self-referencing canonical on each original public page and maintain consistent internal links. Tracking parameters or alternate paths should resolve to the intended document identity; declaring a canonical remains a signal rather than an indexing guarantee.

### Indexability

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/indexability

Whether a page is technically eligible for inclusion in a search index. Eligibility does not guarantee inclusion. Review response status, robots directives, canonical signals, and content availability together. A page can be crawlable but excluded from indexing. Confirm important URLs in the relevant search engine's inspection tools after deployment.

### Crawlability

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/crawlability

Whether a crawler can reach and retrieve a page and the content needed to understand it. Check robots rules, server responses, rendering, and infrastructure restrictions on important public URLs. Allowing a user agent in robots.txt is insufficient if a firewall still challenges requests or the content requires authentication to read.

### Prompt map

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/prompt-map

An organized set of buyer questions linked to audiences, decision stages, target pages, and evidence requirements. Each entry should identify a meaningful decision, its primary URL, and the missing proof. Keep a stable subset for repeated engine observations, then add new questions deliberately so changes in coverage remain interpretable.

### Citation baseline

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/baseline

A dated set of observed answers recorded under documented conditions before evaluating subsequent changes. Save exact prompts, engines, modes, dates, answer excerpts, and cited URLs. Distinguish completed checks from failures. A stable baseline supports comparison across releases without converting a single favorable answer into a durable ranking claim.

### AI referral

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/referral

A visit for which available analytics attributes the source to an AI service. Attribution can be incomplete. Inspect available source, medium, referrer, landing page, and campaign data before assigning a channel. Preserve missing attribution as unknown, and record buyer-reported AI discovery separately from a technically observed referral visit.

### Answer-first content

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/answer-first

A page structure that addresses the reader's central question promptly, then provides evidence, qualifications, detail, and an appropriate next step. A useful section states the answer clearly, identifies its scope, and adds concrete proof or a worked example. Concise summaries help readers evaluate relevance, while the remaining page supplies the depth needed for a buying decision.

### Internal linking

Canonical: https://aeoba.com/resources/glossary/internal-link

Contextual connections between related pages on the same website, helping readers and crawlers discover the next useful destination. Use descriptive anchor text where the destination supplies relevant detail or a useful next step. Connect explanations with their primary service or tool page, and review orphaned pages and broken anchors as the content library expands.
